I switched from a Samsung mobile to an HTC mobile last Christmas. I had been using Samsung Pay during all my time with a Samsung, and it was a great experience. *I never once had a problem while I was using Samsung Pay.* So, I was looking forward to an equal experience with Google Pay... and for a while it was great. For about eight months I used Google Pay everyday. All the retailers around where I work take electronic payment, and I used my HTC mobile to use rewards cards, gift cards, and to pay for items. Every day. After about eight months, Google Pay stopped working, literally over night. One day I was able to use it, the next I was not. When I followed the links I found that my mobile was "not considered secure." enough. It was secure enough the day before, but now it was not. No one can tell me why. All my apps were either pre-installed at the factory, or were downloaded from the PlayStore. No apps from anywhere else. Nothing changed on my mobile from the one day to the next. So, it appears that Google decided arbitrarily to deny me service for no good reason. I installed this app and gave Google a window into my purchasing habits with the understanding that they would, in turn, provide me a service. I no longer am receiving a service from Google in the form of Google Pay, but Google still has the means to track my purchase history. It appears to me that Google has breached the agreement that *they provide me a service in exchange for that information.*. I'm wondering if that agreement is considered to be a contract, and I'm wondering if that contract - implied or explicit - puts Google in an actionable position. I will be keeping an eye out for class-action lawsuits in the hopes of adding my name to it.
